# Independent audit: paired-support addition and response alternative

Source: `candidate 72f4da765f84d146`.
Underlying radial theorem also checked in
`candidate 6748c967393345b9`.


fixed-cap responses. It does not linearize moving-cut branch selectors,
prove a favorable cover, or rule out the opposing stress certificate.
Only a harmless definition clarification was requested: use m>=1 for
the row simplex and N>=1 in the baseline average; the zero action is
treated separately.

## 1. Actual geometry and the contact maximum

The old inequalities are global supporting inequalities of the original
canonical hull. They hold on each displayed fiber by assumption; their
affine dependence on the base and linear dependence on x extends them
to its full convex hull. Adding the zero-field support family for each
base leaves every deformed body unchanged, since those inequalities
already hold on the entire original hull.

At the SAME continuous normal u, averaging N old support right sides
keeps the left coefficient exactly u. Each new slack is the average of
nonnegative old slacks. Thus it vanishes exactly when all components
vanish. At every base and normal each old action has at least one
active zero-field support, so the Cartesian product of active sets is
nonempty. Finite nonnegative coefficients, including zero, then give

 max_(all active tuples) sum_j t_j V_(j,i_j)
     =sum_j t_j max_(old active i_j) V_(j,i_j).

This is the sum of OLD maxima, rather than the maximum of a mere union
of old fields. The distinction is exactly what the paired baselines
implement.

Every combined field is finite, continuous, nonnegative and convex in
the full physical variables. There are finitely many index tuples and
one compact normal sphere. Their uniform bound gives an inner homothet
in every old fiber. Consequently small-e bodies are genuine convex
subsets of the original hull, with every old fiber positive and with
exactly the same projection. No independent facet-velocity feasibility
or hull-repair step is assumed.

For the nonsmooth first variation, at a regular radial endpoint the
new supporting normal has a unique limit. Any sequence of active new
cuts has old slack tending to zero, hence belongs in the limit to the
same active Cartesian product. Conversely each old active tuple gives
the corresponding lower radial loss bound. These two inequalities
give exactly the maximum above divided by the radial support height.
The inner-homothet bound dominates the shell integral. Thus the earlier
radial theorem applies without a continuous contact indicator or a
smooth surface assumption, including d=1.

## 2. Responses and convex-cone closure

Total loss and every fixed closed ambient-halfspace loss integrate the
same physical speed against fixed selectors. Therefore all coordinates
(D,C_1,...,C_m) add exactly. Proper cuts use their interior trace;
inside supporting cuts retain all removed mass and outside supporting
cuts retain none. Pure integer cuts use actual closed full/empty fiber
status. These selectors do not change between the actions, since the
old body and the halfspaces are fixed.

The finite construction remains within the stated action class. It
therefore proves closure under every finite nonnegative combination,
not merely a limit point in a formal response cone. The small parameter
is chosen only after all finitely many fields and coefficients are
fixed, which is sufficient even without a uniformly bounded action
class.

## 3. Finite and arbitrary-menu alternatives

The finite minimax is ordinary convex separation of a finite response
polytope from an open orthant. Its mixture is physically realized by
the paired-support construction, rather than being a random center.

For an arbitrary action class, finite conic combinations define the
cone C. If C misses the strictly positive orthant, its closure also
misses that open set. Separation, together with the two cone scaling
operations and zero in C, gives a nonzero lambda with lambda.C<=0 and
lambda nonnegative on the positive orthant. Thus lambda has nonnegative
coordinates and can be normalized to sum one. This proves the exact
alternative without asserting C itself closed or a global game value
attained.

The finite-subcover argument is independently correct: if every lambda
has one strictly positive pairing, these open sets cover the compact
probability simplex. A finite subcover gives a continuous finite maximum
whose minimum is strictly positive. Finite minimax then yields one
strictly positive response mixture. Caratheodory preserves the response
with at most m+1 actions, or preserves D and all separate losses with
at most m+2. There is no hidden uniform positivity assumption on the
original uncountable menu.

## 4. Exact fixed-cover implication and moving-cut limitation

An actual cover of the original mixed set remains a cover of every
nested new body. If all critical covering masses have positive signed
response C_j-beta D, their normalized masses become strictly smaller
than beta. Fixed strict slack persists in the remaining covering rows.
Taking the largest mass in this finite cover bounds the global maximum
depth from above. This is a valid strict-descent implication involving
all ambient orientations and boundary statuses.

Moving halfspaces require their own actual first variations, with the
existing supporting-facet min/max branches. Body-speed additivity does
not commute with those branches or change the order of existential and
universal allocations. Nor does this fixed-cover alternative produce
a cover. Those limits are correctly explicit in the source.

## 5. Exact physical retained-cap consequence

One additional consequence follows from the already proved variation
formula in `candidate cb7ea417552f0084`.
The paired construction adds every fixed hinge-weighted boundary cost.
If prescribed mark velocities also add, then the retained-mass right
derivative is additive at a noncentroid source. At a centroid it is
superadditive, since

 min_u sum_j t_j Phi_j(u)>=sum_j t_j min_u Phi_j(u).

Equivalently this follows from subadditivity of the exact centroid
gauge penalty. For a polyhedral centroid source, keeping all vertices
of its compact optimal-hinge polar gives finitely many LINEAR response
rows. These can be appended to a finite response vector. This provides
an actual physical secondary test, but still gives no deepest-path
continuation or exact primary-level preservation.

## 6. Actual distinct-contact calibration

Take integer bases -1,0,1 with interval fibers of radii 1,2,1 centered
at zero. This is a complete convex family. The first action cuts with
|x|+e<=2+z, the second with |x|+e<=2-z. Their two-endpoint physical
speeds on the three fibers are respectively (1,1,0) and (0,1,1).
Augment each with zero-field supports 2+z, 2-z and 2.

For coefficients t_1,t_2>=0, the paired construction gives exact small-e
radii

       (1-e t_1, 2-e(t_1+t_2), 1-e t_2).

The fixed oblique cap x+z>=0 has an outside supporting trace at -1,
a proper trace at 0, and an inside supporting trace at 1. Its exact
first loss is t_1+3t_2, the sum of the two old responses. This checks
different contact sets and both supporting statuses in one actual body.
The separate checker evaluates every new Cartesian cut explicitly;
it is supplementary to the general proof.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
